general_information.Description: This course, "Research for Designers," dives into the world of strategic design research. Students will explore qualitative and quantitative research techniques, the importance of data-driven design, and ethical considerations within the research process. This course teaches how to integrate these insights into design thinking, producing evidence-based solutions that resonate with the target audience. By the end of the course, students will gain essential skills in critical analysis, research methodology, empathy building, evidence-based decision-making, and clear communication of findings. This course will transform students into more strategic, insightful, and user-focused designers, ready to tackle the complexities of real-world design challenges. The course can also help students apply the knowledge they have gained in delivering scientific reports and build and develop report presentation skills at seminars and conferences.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/) for up-to-date information and material of the course.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Explain the importance of conducting human-centric research before making design decision, as well as basic definition of design research and design thinking
Apply essentials of design research to conduct a research proposal
Analyse different research methods and the level of appropriation of each method
Create a research plan logically and execute properly
Deliver the research report in a logical and easy-to-understand manner to other stakeholders
Demonstrate professionalism in conducting research and show respect for intellectual properties

assessments.Grading Guide: From session 3 to 18 - Group Presentation Requirements Group size: Each group consists of 4–6 students. Preparation: Work at home based on the course textbook and topics assigned by the instructor. Presentation: In-class presentation of 25–30 minutes, followed by 5–10 minutes Q&A. AI usage: AI tools are allowed (for research, analysis, slide design, images, charts, etc.), but the final work must demonstrate critical thinking, creativity, and originality. Topics: Design as Practice, Research, and Thinking Research Essentials Ethnographic Research Qualitative Research Quantitative Research Visual Research Presenting Your Research Submit: a.
